traceability.evidence:
Story file exists and is referenced throughout implementation and tests: - docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md (spec under assessment)
Core rules implementing the story: - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts - JSDoc: `@story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` and `@req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED`. - ESLint RuleModule with `meta.schema` supporting options `scope` and `exportPriority` using shared `DEFAULT_SCOPE` and `EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES`. - `messages.missingStory` is a clear, actionable error message including function name and an example story path. - `create(context)` reads options, defaults `scope` and `exportPriority`, builds a closure `shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority)`, and passes it to `buildVisitors`. - src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts - JSDoc: `@story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` and requirements `REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED`, `REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION`, `REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT`, `REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE`, `REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY`. - Options type and schema use `DEFAULT_SCOPE` and `EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES` (imported from require-story-helpers), so both rules share the same scope/exportPriority semantics. - Visitors defined for FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression (skipping MethodDefinition), MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature; each calls `runCheck(node)` which first checks `shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority)` then calls `checkReqAnnotation`. - `messages.missingReq` provides a specific, guided message with example `@req` usage and includes `functionName` in the data payload.
Shared detection scope and export priority (REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY): - src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts - `export const DEFAULT_SCOPE: string[] = ["FunctionDeclaration","FunctionExpression","MethodDefinition","TSMethodSignature","TSDeclareFunction"]` – exactly the function-like constructs listed in the story (minus arrow functions, which are explicitly excluded by default). - `export const EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES = ["all", "exported", "non-exported"]`. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts - `function shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority = "all")`: checks `scope.includes(node.type)` and uses `isExportedNode` plus `exportPriority` to gate enforcement, providing a shared, consistent scope mechanism. - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts and src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts both depend on these helpers, ensuring consistent behavior.
JSDoc/comment parsing and error location (REQ-JSDOC-PARSING, REQ-ERROR-LOCATION): - For @story: - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts - `jsdocHasStory`, `commentsBeforeHasStory`, `leadingCommentsHasStory` parse JSDoc and surrounding comments for `@story`. - `hasStoryAnnotation` composes those plus `linesBeforeHasStory`, `parentChainHasStory`, and `fallbackTextBeforeHasStory` (from require-story-io), safely wrapped in try/catch. - `extractName` walks node and parents to produce a function/method name or "(anonymous)"; `reportMissing` and `reportMethod` use this to set `data: { name, functionName: name }` and supply a node (`id` or `key` identifier where possible) so errors are reported at the function or method name location, satisfying REQ-ERROR-LOCATION and user experience criteria. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-io.ts - Implements IO helpers (`linesBeforeHasStory`, `parentChainHasStory`, `fallbackTextBeforeHasStory`) that search surrounding source text and comments for `@story` or `@supports` markers, with guards for missing APIs and malformed ranges. - For @req: - src/utils/annotation-checker.ts - `getJsdocComment`, `getLeadingComments`, `getCommentsBefore`, `combineComments` implement a parallel JSDoc/comment parsing strategy. - `checkReqAnnotation(context, node, options)` retrieves source code, gathers comments, calls `hasReqAnnotation` (from reqAnnotationDetection), and calls `reportMissing` when no annotation is found. - `reportMissing` uses `getNodeName` to compute a human-readable name, constructs `messageId: "missingReq"` and `data: { name, functionName: name }`, and attaches the report to either the identifier/key or the node itself, fulfilling REQ-ERROR-LOCATION and error-message quality requirements. - src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts - `commentContainsReq`, `linesBeforeHasReq`, `parentChainHasReq`, `fallbackTextBeforeHasReq`, and `hasReqAnnotation` mirror the story-side strategy, considering both `@req` and `@supports` and reusing `LOOKBACK_LINES` and `FALLBACK_WINDOW` from require-story-io, meeting REQ-JSDOC-PARSING and REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT while handling edge cases defensively.
TypeScript support and integration (REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT, Integration AC): - TypeScript constructs are explicitly handled: - src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts defines visitors for `TSDeclareFunction` and `TSMethodSignature` that call `helperReportMissing`/`helperReportMethod`. - src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts has listeners `TSDeclareFunction(node)` and `TSMethodSignature(node)` that call `runCheck(node)` and then `checkReqAnnotation`. - Tests: - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts includes TS-specific valid and invalid cases using `withTsLanguageOptions`, e.g. annotated and unannotated `declare function tsDecl(): void;` and interface `method()` signatures. - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts uses `runAnnotationCheckerTests("require-req-annotation", ...)` and `withTsLanguageOptions` to assert correct behavior for TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature when @req is present or missing. - Jest output shows all of these TS-specific tests passing.
Arrow function behavior: - DEFAULT_SCOPE does not include "ArrowFunctionExpression" (src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts), so by default neither rule enforces arrow functions, matching the requirement that arrow functions are excluded by default. - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts includes "[REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED] unannotated arrow function allowed by default" (valid) and shows that arrow exports can be configured via exportPriority tests, confirming the intended default exclusion while still allowing configuration in the future.
Error handling and edge cases (Error Handling AC): - src/rules/helpers/require-story-io.ts and src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts extensively guard against missing `sourceCode.lines`, missing `node.loc`, malformed `range`, missing `getText` or `getCommentsBefore`, and wrap scanning logic in try/catch blocks, returning `false` instead of throwing. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts `hasStoryAnnotation` is fully wrapped in try/catch to avoid breaking lint runs on unexpected data. - src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts `hasReqAnnotation` uses try/catch around advanced heuristics and falls back to simple JSDoc/comment inspection if anything fails. - tests/rules/require-story-io.edgecases.test.ts directly verifies: - `linesBeforeHasStory` returns false when `source.lines` or `node.loc` is missing or invalid. - `fallbackTextBeforeHasStory` returns false when `getText` or `node.range` is missing. - `parentChainHasStory` behaves correctly when parent comments do or do not contain `@story`.
Documentation with examples and configuration (Documentation AC): - docs/rules/require-story-annotation.md - Documents purpose, supported node types (including TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature), options schema (scope and exportPriority) with defaults and JSON schema, configuration samples, correct/incorrect examples, and TypeScript-specific examples. - Contains `@story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` and `@req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED`, tying it back to this story. - docs/rules/require-req-annotation.md - Similarly documents node types, configuration, and JS/TS examples, and explicitly states that semantics and defaults mirror `require-story-annotation`, demonstrating consistent behavior across both rules.
Tests explicitly referencing this story and requirements, all passing (Testable AC, Core Functionality AC): - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts - File header: `Tests for: docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` and `@req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED`. - Covers valid and invalid cases for all function-like constructs in DEFAULT_SCOPE plus arrow functions (ensuring they are allowed by default unless configured), and includes exportPriority and scope option behavior. - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts - File header referencing this story and requirements `REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED`, `REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION`, `REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT`, `REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS`, with comprehensive valid/invalid cases including TS constructs and all exportPriority/scope permutations. - tests/utils/annotation-checker.test.ts and tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts jointly validate @req detection helpers and their TS support. - `npm test -- --verbose` (run via `jest --ci --bail --verbose`) reports: - PASS for "Require Story Annotation Rule (Story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS)". - PASS for "Require Req Annotation Rule (Story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS)". - PASS for helper suites: "Require Story Helpers", "Require Story IO helpers - edge cases", "Require Story Core" (including autofix behavior), and `annotation-checker`/`reqAnnotationDetection` tests. - Overall summary: `Test Suites: 36 passed, 36 total` and `Tests: 277 passed, 277 total`.
Taken together, these implementations, tests, and docs show that all acceptance criteria and detailed requirements in docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md are satisfied.
traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS are met. The two core rules `require-story-annotation` and `require-req-annotation` share a common detection scope and exportPriority semantics, enforce their respective annotations on the same set of function-like constructs (excluding arrow functions by default), support TypeScript-specific forms, and use aligned JSDoc/comment parsing strategies. Error messages are clear and actionable, error locations target function/method names, edge cases and malformed inputs are handled gracefully, and there is comprehensive rule documentation with examples and configuration options. Multiple dedicated test suites reference this story and its requirement IDs and all of them pass in the Jest run, confirming correct and complete implementation.
